newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-BUNDESBANK SIGNALS MONETARY POLICY ON HOLD.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BUNDESBANK SIGNALS MONETARY POLICY ON HOLD.

text.p: The Bundesbank on Tuesday set a tender for 14-day securities repurchase agreements, or repos, at an unchanged fixed rate of 3.00 percent, signalling that its monetary policy stance remains unchanged for the time being.

Financial markets had speculated that the Bundesbank might depart from its policy of setting fixed-rate repo tenders at the three percent interest rate to support the mark against the dollar and other European currencies.

But speculation of a repo rate move, which had been quite intense last week, had been dampened in recent days because the dollar had eased off an eight-year high of just over 1.89 marks it reached last week.

Markets nonetheless expect the central bank to raise rates some time in the coming months. Speculation on a move is now likely to shift to the central bank's next policy-making council meeting on August 21.

The new securities repurchase pact will offset a repo pact totalling 79.4 billion marks, set at a fixed rate of 3.00 percent which expires on Wednesday. The repo rate has been held at three percent for the last year.
Analysts warned that with financial markets now convinced that German monetary policy was about to tighten after five years of lower rates, speculation would remain rife.
July inflation data released on Tuesday showed annual inflation was running at 1.9 percent, just below the two percent level the Bundesbank considers tolerable.
But that figure was also the highest since June 1995, backing up a recent comment from Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing that price trends are moving in the wrong direction.

Uwe Angenendt, an economist at BHF-Bank, noted that the Bundesbank could theoretically change its policy stance when it sets its next regular tender next week, but he said he believed this was unlikely.

"The Bundesbank's cautious stance remains intact because it has only set a repo tender for this week, so speculation regarding a repo move has only been postponed until next week's tender announcement," he said.

"But I don't think they'll change the tender next week so soon before the Bundesbank's next council meeting on August 21. ... The Bundesbank is clearly reserving the option to decide on its repo policy from week to week.
We see the repo rate rising to 3.50 percent by the end of the year.
Joerg Kraemer at Merrill Lynch said of the decision: "It was expected. The Bundesbank will not start the rate hike process without broad-based support on the council."
"I see a 75 percent chance that the Bundesbank will start the rate hike process within the next three months," he added.

German bond or Bund futures ticked higher after the announcement, the September Bund future trading at 102.10 at 0730 GMT, up from 101.91 at Monday's close. German shares saw little reaction, continuing to trade firmer.

The Bundesbank itself triggered speculation that its policy was about to turn two weeks ago, when it went into its summer break deliberately leaving its policy options open for the second half of the four-week period.

In a break with recent tradition, the central bank announced the conditions for the first two repos during the four-week period but held off on the announcement of conditions at which it would offer funds to the market in the third week until today's announcement.
Over the last year the Bundesbank has consistently announced its repo tenders in advance, immediately after its regular council meetings.
